# FLOAT64 RANGE boundaries at finite overflow and adjacent representable values.
# Check whether crossing the finite limit includes infinity; these counts also distinguish
# overflow boundaries from a bound exactly equal to infinity.
SELECT ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT(id, n) ORDER BY id) FROM (SELECT id, COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY x RANGE BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 1.7976931348623157e308 FOLLOWING) AS n FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, -1.7976931348623157e308 AS x), (2, 0.0), (3, 1.7976931348623157e308), (4, CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64))]))
?>

SELECT ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT(id, n) ORDER BY id) FROM (SELECT id, COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY x DESC RANGE BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND 1.7976931348623157e308 FOLLOWING) AS n FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, 1.7976931348623157e308 AS x), (2, 0.0), (3, -1.7976931348623157e308), (4, CAST('-inf' AS FLOAT64))]))
?>

SELECT ARRAY_AGG(STRUCT(id, n) ORDER BY id) FROM (SELECT id, COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY x RANGE BETWEEN 0.0000000000000002220446049250313 PRECEDING AND 0.0000000000000002220446049250313 FOLLOWING) AS n FROM UNNEST([STRUCT(1 AS id, 0.9999999999999999 AS x), (2, 1.0), (3, 1.0000000000000002), (4, 1.0000000000000004)]))
?>

# Record BigQuery's exact error messages for NaN and infinite offsets.
DECLARE offset_value FLOAT64 DEFAULT CAST('nan' AS FLOAT64);
SELECT COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY x RANGE BETWEEN CURRENT ROW AND offset_value FOLLOWING) FROM UNNEST([1.0]) AS x
?>

DECLARE offset_value FLOAT64 DEFAULT CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64);
SELECT COUNT(*) OVER (ORDER BY x RANGE BETWEEN offset_value PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) FROM UNNEST([1.0, CAST('inf' AS FLOAT64)]) AS x
?>
